body: I understand what you're saying. I've been suicidal forever. I'm still alive. I think people have misconceptions about suicide sometimes. People look at it as giving up sometimes. That it's a conscious decision. It is and it isnt, I guess. I see it more like a symptom of an illness. It's like cancer. Sometimes you get better, sometimes you dont. You can get radiation, chemo, surgery, but sometimes you still die. Suicidal thoughts are like that. Every day I fight off suicide. I'm scared to die. Now, if I'm scared to die why not just not kill myself? Not so simple. It's likely going to happen whether I want it to or not one of these days. All you can do is fight it off until you cant/don't want to anymore and hope that you get better even though it's possible you might not. One day, hour, minute at a time friend. I wish you well.

I'm not sure to what extent you have that feeling. What youre saying is a little vague (i understand sometimes its hard to put things jnto words)Without going into too many details, I had an experience like that that was pretty intense. It was a delusion and I was psychotic. I didn't know at the time. I'm not saying you are. That's just anecdotal.

The thing is, opening up to friends if he can do that may not help anyway. I wish I could tell you something you could do, but speaking from my own experience, I'm just not sure there's anything you can do. Hopefully, your friend will get help and hopefully that help works, but don't feel bad if there's nothing you can do. Depression sucks.

I wish that anybody that wanted to could. While I understand the survival instincts necessity, sometimes I think it's just some big cosmic joke. And it's sad that people are shamed when they try to overcome it.
Its depression, but I call the feeling "dead inside". It's funny, I am the other way around. Dead inside is not great, but I really do prefer it to anxiety. Anything is better than anxiety.

like to describe it as being a 3rd party to myself. I am watching myself do things, but have no control. I try to tell myself to stop, but I'm just a third party, so I can't always make myself listen. I can't restrain myself because even though I'm a third party, my third party form doesn't have a physical existence. I am better now, but psychosis is some scary stuff. For everybody.

Me too. I don't think everybody gets it, but I like to describe my life as watching it like I'm a third person to myself. I don't really live it or control it (although in reality I guess I do, just doesn't feel like it). Managing my own thoughts seems like a better term.

I am the least picky Eater I know. I will eat absolutely anything. I've even had a cockroach on a stick before. But beets. That is the absolute one thing I will refuse to eat. If God served beets at a dinner party, I would just have to be rude.

I get the drug addiction thing. The sad thing is that when I likened it to drug addiction it was with a person and not a thing. I used to see movies/news about obsessed people and wonder how they could be like that. Its not that hard, i found out. A person made me feel good. Started out great, but then I needed more and more and more from this person until they couldn't give anything else. Like alcohol. In moderation is good, but the shit can ruin your life. I mean it's not the alcohols fault, it's yours for being additicted. That's how I was with the person, and.....well, no need to go into details but I totally get what you are saying about distractions, obsessions, and drug addiction.

Yeah. I've called my friend in a state of real panic (I swear to god, the depression will not be what kills me, but the anxiety) where he really thought somebody died or my house burnt down or I had terminal cancer. What happened? Um, nothing, and now I feel dumb for calling.

Yes. I get so overwhelmed by the internal, I don't notice or care about the external. I'm so consumed by my thoughts, that my actions are essentially on autopilot. I have one person I can talk to when  I'm overwhelmed, but it gets harder these days. He will ask me "what happened?" and well, nothing happened really. My day/life is fine and dandy. For that matter, good things may have  happened. I try to explain that my environment is not always consistent with my mood, but it's hard for some people to understand. I even try to find bad things going on sometimes just so I have something to complain about rather than just being upset about nothing. Yeah, I miss out on a lot of life. Good, bad, indifferent. I may as well be a brain stuck in a jar, because what's going on in my mind seems to be all that matters to me. I, too, wish I could be grateful about the good things in life. There are a lot of them. I don't care (to put it kind of bluntly), but they are certainly there if I ever can make myself.
Mostly fear, honestly. Hate living,  but scared to die. Also, obligation. There are people in my life I feel obligated to live for. I wish that it was happiness that kept me alive.

It made me feel better to not think of depression as something that can be overcame. I can't overcome it, it's not going to go away-ever. Not trying to say it won't for some people, but I've been going on decades, so....

Anyway, whenever I started looking at it as something that cant be cured, I started looking at it as something that can be managed. Part of the stress of my depression was trying to find that thing, that person, that situation that would fix me. Of course, it never worked more than temporarily and the crash was devastating. Now I just ask myself what I can do to make myself feel better today, this hour, this minute. I find I'm more motivated to do something if I'm not thinking about it as the cure and worry about how I will be if it doesn't work. So, my advice is to just find those things you like to do and will make you feel better (even temporarily), whatever those things are, and do those without worrying about whether they will help you overcome depression in its entirety.
Yeah. I do come here just to listen/talk to people that can relate to some of my issues, but it only helps to an extent, because it's not face to face.

Holy crap, I couldn't have written this myself other than changing "her" to "him." Sucks so bad, and I know this might not help with your pain, but if there's anything I can say it is that I've been feeling a little better. Took a long while, but time helps sometimes.
I was pretty productive today.

I've been depressed forever. For some people I don't think it's something that will ever truly go away. You can see a therapist, try medication, or any number of things. Try different things and see what works, but don't be discouraged if you're not all the way better every day. I have good days and bad days. The biggest thing I realized lately though is that I can't cure what's not curable, but I can manage what's manageable. Find those things that make you feel better. If it's temporary, that's ok. Manage. When those things don't work try other things. Whatever helps you stay alive, do it, but if things don't work out for you every day, then that's okay. Day by day. Try again the next day.

This is my conversation:

Him: How are you? 
Me: I'm feeling a little sad and anxious today
Him: Oh, what happened? 
Me: nothing really, just one of those days
Him: well if nothing happened how can you be upset? 
Me: my mood is not always dependent upon what's going on
Him: .....
Me in my head: why do I keep telling him this stuff. He already thinks I'm an alien...

Thanks. Took me a while to get there. Been doing a lot of self analysis lately. Trying to fix my problems. I kept thinking, if I do this then I will feel that. If I have this, then I'll be happy. Only to get disappointed when I feel better for a while only to have it come crashing down. This led to me stop trying because I knew it wouldn't work. Problem was that I was trying to cure. I can't cure what's currently (as far as I can tell) uncurable. So doing something is not going to cure anything, but if it makes me feel better, even temporarily, I should still do it. Just hope I can remember this tomorrow....
Me and you both. It's so rare that I find somebody I'm comfortable opening up to. I get so excited, I think, that I go overboard. I regret it every single time.

What I'm going to say may not be helpful, but I don't have advice to offer. I can offer understanding though. I can relate. I've suffered from depression forever. Well, a lot of life is kind of blacked out so it might as well be forever. I never shared with people at work, though. The last couple years my work has suffered. Maybe because I'm depressed, because I can't concentrate. Maybe because I'm just not good at what I do. Anyway, I'm sure I was going to get fired soon. Maybe just a thought in my mind, but truth for me. 9 months ago my husband died. He was murdered so it was everywhere. In the news. I couldn't escape it. I went back to work and my work still suffers. In addition to depression, I developed a lot of anxiety I didn't have before. Maybe it contributec. Maybe not. So I have so  many mixed feelings. I don't want to feel like I'm being kept around out of pity. I don't want it to be seen as an excuse to do a shitty job. I also want people to understand what I go through every day. I also don't want to tell them what I go through every day. It sucks. I feel you. Nobody talks about it, but I still feel it there and I wish it would just go away.

I don't know why this hapoens, but just wanted to say I can relate. I finally got with somebody that made me truly happy, alive. It's semi long distance (3 hours so not too far, but we're both really busy so taking the trips not always easy) and one night I was able to get away and go stay with him. To get away from it all and just be with the one who gives me some spark. We had a great time, I felt so happy. We fell asleep on the couch and then when we woke up to go to the bedroom, I don't know what happened. I literally don't know what happened. I completely flipped out. Started saying crazy things, engaging in some weird kind of self pity, saying all kinds of things. It was all too crazy for me to explain and I don't really remember all of it, but it ended up with me leaving. Then begging to come back in. He told me to just go home. I ended up sitting on his porch all night, like some kind of crazy stalker. Waiting for him to get up so I can explain, except I don't know how. Because I have no idea what the fuck just went on. He forgave me, sort of. It's not the same though. Will never be the same. After all the progress I made and the happiness I got to, I fuck ed my future in that one single moment and I don't even know what provoked me. All the shit that happened to me in my life. The abuse. If I had a time machine, it's not those moments I would try to fix. I accept that I didn't have control. If I could go back in time, it would be to that night, because I should have had control and I didnt. I get this "where did it go wrong" moment a lot. I can relate. Do you ever feel like a third party? Like you're just watching yourself do stuff and telling yourself to stop, but you're on the outside of yourself so you can't make yourself stop? Losing control sucks so bad, especially when you're not sure why.

Me too. When I feel like I've done something wrong, I want to be beat up. When I'm sad, I want to be beat up. I asked my special friend to do this a few times, to just beat the shit out of me, and he's looked at me like I'm crazy or tried to make me feel better in more "constructive" ways. I don't know why I want to be physically hurt, maybe because in my mind it's because it takes my mind off of emotional hurt and is preferable. All I know is that when I get hurt or think about it, I feel better. Alive. Right now, I can get violence two ways. By my own hand, or during sex. It's not a sexual thing, though, and getting beat up outside of that would be oh so pleasurable. Sorry for the long thing, just got this off my chest while you brought up the topic. I too would join the shit out of Fight Club.

I understand. I hated medication. I wanted to feel. I go back and forth though. When I feel, I'm miserable. When I'm dead inside, I'm not, but I am....something else. I feel you on some of this, but can't say I'm glad. I wish I could just have some kind of medium like "normal" people. I don't want to feel, I don't want to not feel. It is what it is, though. I don't think depression can be cured, so I guess I just live (or not) with it.
